# Introducing the Reject Inference (RI) problem

## The accept-decision induced data missingness

### The acceptance loop

## But, why take care about the rejects?

* **Key observation:** Acceptance decision is **not** random
  $\Rightarrow$ the rejects-distribution (ideally) unequals the accepts-distribution

* Does it then make sense to just ignore them? Or is that leaving potential
  on the table?

* Possible arguments to be able to ignore the observation:

  * **Ignorability:** Training a scorecard on accepts can be expected to be equal to training on accepts
    and rejects
  * It is not possible to gain any information of the probability of default from
    using the rejects information, because
      * There is no relevant information on rejects (**irrelevance**)
      * No method works (**methodologically impossible**)

* A general stochastic model is helpful to check these arguments.

## Some formalization: a stochastic model


### The building blocks of the acceptance loop

At any certain point $t \in \mathbb{N}$ of the acceptance loop, let the following random variables on 
$(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$ generate the "building pieces" of the RI problem

* $X_m^{(t)}$ the model features,
* $X_h^{(t)}$ the hidden features,
* $\varepsilon^{(t)}$ the noise,
* $Y^{(t)}$ the outcomes and
* $Z^{(t)}$ the acceptance decision.

---

### How do they relate to each other?

Letting $\omega \in \Omega$:

* Repayment outcome as the result of a measurable function $\iota_t$

::: {style="text-align: center; margin: -1em 0;"}
$$
Y^{(t)}(\omega) = \iota_t \left(X_m^{(t)}(\omega), X_h^{(t)}(\omega), \varepsilon^{(t)}(\omega) \right) \in \{b, g\}
$$

:::

* The acceptance decision:

::: {style="text-align: center; margin: -1em 0;"}
$$
Z^{(t)}(\omega) = d_t\left(s_t\left(X_m^{(t)}(\omega) \right), X_h^{(t)}(\omega) \right) \in \{a, r\}
$$
$$
\Rightarrow Y^{(t)} \perp\!\!\!\perp Z^{(t)} | X_m^{(t)}, X_h^{(t)}
$$

:::

* And the *observable* repayment outcome

::: {style="text-align: center; margin: -1em 0;"}
$$
Y_m^{(t)}(\omega) = \begin{cases}
  Y^{(t)}(\omega) & Z^{(t)}(\omega) = a \\
  \mathtt{na}  & Z^{(t)}(\omega) = r
\end{cases}
$$

:::

---

### What about the dynamic view? Bridging the RVs to the data

* The historic data can be seen as a realization of the family

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: -1em; margin-bottom: 0.5em;"}
$$
\bigcup_{\tau = 0}^{t-1} \left\{\left(X_{m,i}^{(\tau)}, X_{h,i}^{(\tau)}, Y_{i}^{(\tau)}, Z^{(\tau)}_i \right)\right\}_{i=1}^{N_\tau}
$$

:::
  
:::{style="padding-left: 2rem;"}
which will be denoted as $\left(X_m^{:t}, X_h^{:t}, Y^{:t}, Z^{:t} \right)$
:::

* Then the scorecard $s_t$ can be seen as the result of a (measurable) learning
  procedure $a_t$ mapping from $\left(X_m^{:t}, X_h^{:t}, Y^{:t}, Z^{:t} \right)$
  to the space of admissible scorecards

## So can we ignore the missingness?

### When do we have ignorability?

There are three general cases of missingness mechanism [@littleAndRubingAnalysisWithMissingData]
with different implications on ignorability

::: {style="text-align: center;  margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1.5em;"}

| Type | Definition | Missingess ignorable? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCAR | $Z^{(t)} \perp\!\!\!\perp X_m^{:t}, X_h^{:t}, Y^{:t}$ | Yes |
| MAR | $Z^{(t)} | X_m^{:t} \perp\!\!\!\perp X_h^{:t}, Y^{:t}$ | Yes for well-specified ML methods |
| MNAR | $Z^{(t)} | X_m^{:t} \cancel{\perp\!\!\!\perp} X_h^{:t}, Y^{:t}$ | No |

:::

**Recall:** Per definition of $Y^{(t)}$, $Z^{(t)}$ and $s_t$ it always holds (given all past $d_t$)
$$
Z^{(t)} | X_m^{:t}, X_h^{:t} \perp\!\!\!\perp Y^{:t}
$$

---

### And what about irrelevance and methodological impossiblity?

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="37%"}

**Irrelevance:** It would be given if for all $t$

* Equality in distribution, i. e.
  $``\mathbb{P}_{Y^{(t)} | X^{(t)}, Z^{(t)}=a} = \mathbb{P}_{Y^{(t)} | X^{(t)}, Z^{(t)}=r}"$

* $\mathbb{P}_{Y^{(t)} | X^{(t)}, Z^{(t)}=r}$ too noisy

:::

::: {.column width="4%"}


:::

::: {.column width="59%"}

**Methodological impossibility:**

* Unclear whether/when RI works.

* @ehrhardt2021rejectReview: Most augmentation inconsistent,
  equivalent to ignoring rejects or base on questionable assumptions:

    * tend to base solely on $\mathbb{P}_{Y^{(t)} | X^{(t)}, Z^{(t)}=a}$
    * $\Rightarrow$ implicitly assume equality in distribution.

* Other methods exist based on extra assumptions - still in research or abandoned.^[
  E.g. @Li_et_al_2017_semisupervised_svm, @Mancisdor_et_al_2020_DeepGenM_for_RI,
  @Anderson2019_BayesianNetForRI or @bansikCrook2007
]   

:::

::::

# Surprisingly, the bias might be (indirectly) observable

## Motivation

* @kozdoi_et_al_BE_BASL report promising results regarding in the
  RI milleau for unbiased scorecard evaluation.

    * They report scorecard evaluation on accepts overestimating the
      performance w.r.t. a complete holdout population

    * Augmenting the sample with rejects seems to deliver more realistic
      results.

* So we can ask:

  * Can we see such incongruence in a world of "only accepts"?

  * If so: can we use that as a proxy for the bias?

## Formulating the hypothesis

### Defining the surprise

* Let the "expectation" be the (cross validated) performance
  measured over historic data.

* Let the "realization" be the performance measured over
  new accepts.

* The surprise is then the differnce between expectation and realization.

### Hypothesis

* Assuming that

  * For an unbiased scorecard and threshold choosing method, the surprise
    is usually almost zero.
  * For the biased counterpart the absolute surprise is large

* The minimization of the surprise can be used as a reward signal
  to train an estimator for $\mathbb{P}_{Y^{(t)} | X^{(t)}, Z^{(t)}=r}$

## A "theoretical" motivation for the hypothesis assumptions:

### An unsurprising setting

Assume a "stationary setting", i.e.

* An applicants without distributional shifts:

::: {style="text-align: center; margin: -1em 0;"}
$$
\forall t \forall i : \left(X_{m,i}^{(\tau)}, X_{h,i}^{(\tau)}, Y_{i}^{(\tau)} \right) \sim \mathbb{P}_{X_m, X_h, Y}
$$

:::

* The missingness is MAR.

* The scorecard model estimators is parametric, ML based and well specified.

* The scorecard learning procedure remains the same $\forall t: a_t = a$

* The method for choosing the acceptance threshold remains the same.

---

### What should then happen?

Then we can expect that

  * The scorecard-model will be roughly constant
  * The same region of the acceptance population gets selected
  * And therefore the history and the new accepts come from the same region
    of the acceptance population.
  * Therefore expectation and realization should be close.

# Designing a simulation framework to test the hypothesis

## Applicant's population

### General DGP

* The classical two class linear discriminant analysis with equal covariances problem was chosen for the simulation.
  
* Let $X = (X_m^\top, X_h^\top)^\top$, then

$$
\underbrace{X | Y = b}_{=: X_b}
\sim \mathcal{N}\left(
  \mu_b  \! = \! \begin{bmatrix}
    \mu_{b, m} \\
    \mu_{b, h}
  \end{bmatrix},
  \Sigma
\right) , \;
\underbrace{X | Y = g}_{=: X_g}
\sim \mathcal{N}\left(
  \mu_g \! = \! \begin{bmatrix}
    \mu_{g, m} \\
    \mu_{g, h}
  \end{bmatrix},
  \Sigma
\right)
$$
  
:::{style="padding-left: 2rem;"}
with  $\mu_{b, m} = (0,0)^\top, \mu_{b, h}=0$,  $\mu_{g, m} = (1,2)^\top, \mu_{g, h}=-1$ and

$$
\Sigma = \begin{pmatrix}
1 & \sigma_{m, 12} & \sigma_{mh} \\
\sigma_{m, 12} & 1 & \sigma_{mh} \\
\sigma_{mh} & \sigma_{mh} & 1
\end{pmatrix} \text{, positive definite}
$$

:::

---

### Choosing suitable covariances

Two bayes-rule based models: restricted (only using $X_m$) and full with error rates
$P^{*}_m$, $P^{*}_e$ respectively

## The acceptance policy

```{python}
## Import what you need and do what you want
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
from berebasl.simulation.credit_data_simulation import CreditData
from berebasl.estimation.classifiers import BatchedLogistic

at_gen = 60
feats, lbls = base_sim_objs["credit_data"].unbiased_obs(up_to_round_idx=at_gen-1)
lr = BatchedLogistic(
  n_features=feats.size(-1),
  batch_shape = torch.Size([]),
  dtype=feats.dtype,
  device=feats.device
)
N = feats.size(0)
torch.manual_seed(1807)
rand_perm_N = torch.randperm(N)
count_train = round(N * 0.7)
train_idxs = rand_perm_N[:count_train]
vali_idxs = rand_perm_N[count_train:]

lr.fit(feats[train_idxs], lbls[train_idxs])

scores_vali = lr.predict_prob_bad(feats[vali_idxs]).squeeze(-1)
lbls_vali = lbls[vali_idxs]

figsize_th = (5, 4.5)

```

* Score-Model: Logistic regression estimated via Newton–Raphson.

* Threshold selection: No cost-sensitive optimization, calculated as mean of 10
  5-fold-cross-validated estimates. Two methods were used:


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=1}
```{python}
#| label: roc-optimal-th
#| fig-cap: "ROC-optimal threshold."
from berebasl.evaluation.batched_metrics import (
  batched_roc_points,
  optimal_roc_thresholds_from_roc_points
)

fpr, tpr, sorted_scores, sorted_targets, sorted_mask_valid = batched_roc_points(scores_vali, lbls_vali, dim=-1)

sq_eucl_to_opt = (
  fpr.square() +
  (tpr-1).square()
)

idx_min_dist = sq_eucl_to_opt.argmin().item()
threshold = round(sorted_scores[idx_min_dist].item(), 2)


plt.figure(figsize=figsize_th)

plt.plot(fpr, tpr, label="ROC", color='C0')
plt.scatter(
  fpr[[idx_min_dist]],
  tpr[[idx_min_dist]],
  label=f"ROC-opt. pt. $\\tau = {threshold}$",
  s=10,
  color='C1',
  zorder=30
)
plt.scatter(
  [0],
  [1],
  label="Best ROC-pt.",
  s=10,
  color='C2',
  zorder=30
)
plt.xlabel("False Positive Rate")
plt.ylabel("True Positive Rate")

plt.legend()

plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: ks-criterion-th
#| fig-cap: "Kolmogorov-Smirnov-criterion threshold."
from berebasl.evaluation.batched_metrics import compute_batched_cdfs_and_sorted

sorted_scores, sorted_mask, cdf_pos, cdf_neg, sorted_targets = compute_batched_cdfs_and_sorted(

)

ks_values = torch.abs(cdf_pos - cdf_neg)
idx_max_ks = ks_values.argmax().item()

plt.figure(figsize=figsize_th)

plt.plot(sorted_scores, cdf_pos, label="$CDF_b$", color='C0', lw=2)
plt.plot(sorted_scores, cdf_neg, label="$CDF_g$", color='C1', lw=2)

x_max_ks = sorted_scores[[idx_max_ks, idx_max_ks]].tolist()
y_max_ks = [cdf_pos[idx_max_ks].item(), cdf_neg[idx_max_ks].item()]

plt.plot(
  x_max_ks,
  y_max_ks,
  color='C2',
  ls="dashed",
  lw=2,
  label=f"$\\tau_{{KS}}={round(sorted_scores[idx_max_ks].item(), 2)}$"
)
plt.scatter(x_max_ks, y_max_ks, color='C2', s=20, zorder=30)

plt.xlabel("Probability of Default")
plt.ylabel("CDF")

plt.legend(loc="upper left")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
| --- | --- | --- |
| Estimation of $s_t = 1 - p_t$ | Full history $\rightarrow p^*_t$ | All Accepts according to biased policy $\rightarrow \tilde{p}_t$ |
| Threshold estimation | CV-based over Full history $\rightarrow \tau^*_t$ | CV based over Accepts according to biased policy $\rightarrow \tilde{\tau}_t$ |
| Accept-Decision before MNAR-overwrites | Accept if $p^*_t < \tau^*_t$, $\rightarrow$ *unbiased accepts* at $t$ | Accept if $\tilde{p}_t < \tilde{\tau}_t$, $\rightarrow$ *biased accepts* at $t$ |
```

### MNAR overrides

With $(p_t, \tau_t) \in \{(p^*_t, \tau^*_t), (\tilde{p}_t, \tilde{\tau}_t)\}$, $\pi_b$, the decision with MNAR overrides:

$$
d\left(x_m, x_h^{(t)} \right) = \begin{cases}
  r & x_h^{(t)} > \operatorname{percentile}_{1-\pi_b/2}(\mathbf{X}_m^{(t)}) \\
  a & x_h^{(t)} < \operatorname{percentile}_{\pi_b/2}(\mathbf{X}_m^{(t)}) \\
  d'(x_m) & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$

whereby

* $\mathbf{X}_m^{(t)}$ the realized hidden features at $t$
* $\operatorname{percentile}_{1}(\mathbf{X}_m^{(t)}) \equiv \max \mathbf{X}_m^{(t)}$
* $\operatorname{percentile}_{0}(\mathbf{X}_m^{(t)}) \equiv \min \mathbf{X}_m^{(t)}$

::: {style="text-align: left; margin-top: -0.8em; margin-bottom: 0em;"}

**Note:** since $-1 = \mu_{h, g} < \mu_{h, b} = 0$ the overrides tend to reject
bads and accept goods. 

:::


# Evidence for the hypothesis

## Checking the biased policy "overfocusing" in a region

```{python}
#| label: acc-rates-setup
#| output: false
import os, json
from experiments.acceptance_loop_cv_based_MNAR import THRESHOLD_BASIS, METRIC_CATEGORIES, EXPECTATION_TYPES, REAL_PERFORMANCE_TYPES

T = len(THRESHOLD_BASIS)
M = len(METRIC_CATEGORIES)
CACHED_IMG_DIR = "_cached_imgs"
IMG_DIR = CACHED_IMG_DIR + "/acc-rates"
USE_CACHED_IMAGES = True
os.makedirs(IMG_DIR, exist_ok=True)

def plot_acceptance_summary(base_sim, idx_wished_corr, img_dir=IMG_DIR):
    """Build the acceptance-rate/threshold figure for one (corr, bias) combo,
    save it to disk, and return (filepath, corr_value, bias_value)."""
    corr_val = base_sim["corr_to_hidden"][idx_wished_corr].item()
    bias_val = base_sim["bias_prop"]

    fname = f"acc_corr_{corr_val:.2f}_bias_{bias_val:.2f}.png".replace("-", "m")
    fpath = os.path.join(img_dir, fname).replace("\\", "/")

    if os.path.exists(fpath) and USE_CACHED_IMAGES:
      if USE_CACHED_IMAGES:
        return fpath, corr_val, bias_val
      else:
        os.remove(fpath)

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(4.5*(T+1) + 0.5, 3*M + 1))
    gs = plt.GridSpec(
        nrows=M+1, ncols=T+1, figure=fig,
        height_ratios=[1]*M + [0.1], wspace=0.3, hspace=0.8
    )
    bad_flag = base_sim["credit_data"].default_flag[idx_wished_corr, :].to(bool)
    gen_round = base_sim["credit_data"].gen_round
    G = gen_round[-1].item() + 1
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("RdBu_r")
    arange_rounds = torch.arange(1, G)
    point_colors = cmap(arange_rounds.numpy())
    tab10_cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab10")
    th_colors = {th: tab10_cmap((i_th+1)*2) for i_th, th in enumerate(THRESHOLD_BASIS)}

    for i_th, th in enumerate(THRESHOLD_BASIS):
        for i_m, m in enumerate(METRIC_CATEGORIES):
            acc_flag = base_sim["alternative_accepted"].get(th + '_' + m, base_sim["credit_data"].accepted)[idx_wished_corr, :]
            count_accepts = gen_round.new_zeros((G,)).scatter_add_(
                dim=0, index=gen_round, src=acc_flag.to(gen_round.dtype))
            count_accepted_bads = gen_round.new_zeros((G,)).scatter_add_(
                dim=0, index=gen_round, src=(bad_flag & acc_flag).to(gen_round.dtype))

            ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[i_m, i_th])
            ax.scatter(count_accepts[1:], count_accepted_bads[1:] / count_accepts[1:], s=5, color=point_colors)
            ax.set_xlabel("# Accepted")
            ax.set_ylabel("Bad rate among Accepts")
            ax.set_title(("Unbiased" if th == "oracle" else "Biased") + " Policy (" + m.upper() + ")")

            if i_th == 0:
                ax_th = fig.add_subplot(gs[i_m, T])
                ax_th.axhline(y=base_sim["data_generator"].prob_bad, ls="dashed", color='k', lw=1, label=r"$\mathbb{P}(Y=b)$")
                for th_b in THRESHOLD_BASIS:
                    thresholds = (
                        base_sim["stats"][th_b + "_" + m + '_thresholds']
                        .mean(dim=(1, 3))[:, idx_wished_corr]
                    )
                    ax_th.plot(arange_rounds - 1, thresholds, color=th_colors[th_b], label=th_b)
                ax_th.set_title("Thresholds based on " + m.upper())
                ax_th.set_ylabel("Threshold")
                ax_th.set_xlabel("Generation Round")

    cbar_ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[-1, :-1])
    sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=plt.Normalize(vmin=1, vmax=G-1), cmap=cmap)
    cbar = fig.colorbar(sm, cax=cbar_ax, orientation="horizontal")
    cbar.set_label("Generation Round")
    cbar.ax.xaxis.set_label_position('top')
    cbar.ax.xaxis.tick_top()

    th_legend_ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[-1, T])
    th_legend_ax.axis('off')
    th_legend_ax.legend(*ax_th.get_legend_handles_labels(), ncols=T+1, loc="lower center",
                         handlelength=1.0, handletextpad=0.4)



    fig.suptitle(f"$\\sigma_{{mh}} = {corr_val:.2f}$, $\\pi_b = {bias_val:.2f}$")

    fig.savefig(fpath, dpi=110, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    return fpath, corr_val, bias_val

def render_selector_html(manifest, container_id, corr_label=r"\sigma_{mh}", bias_label=r"\pi_b"):
    corr_values = sorted(manifest.keys(), key=float)
    bias_values = sorted({b for d in manifest.values() for b in d}, key=float)
    default_corr, default_bias = corr_values[0], bias_values[0]
    default_img = manifest[default_corr][default_bias]

    manifest_json = json.dumps(manifest)
    corr_options = "\n".join(f'<option value="{c}">{c}</option>' for c in corr_values)
    bias_options = "\n".join(f'<option value="{b}">{b}</option>' for b in bias_values)

    html = f"""<figure class="acc-selector" id="{container_id}" data-manifest='{manifest_json}'>
<div class="acc-selector-controls">
<label>${corr_label}$:
<select class="acc-corr-select">{corr_options}</select>
</label>
<label>${bias_label}$:
<select class="acc-bias-select">{bias_options}</select>
</label>
</div>
<img class="acc-selector-img" src="{default_img}" />
</figure>
<script>
(function() {{
var root = document.getElementById('{container_id}');
var manifest = JSON.parse(root.getAttribute('data-manifest'));
function update() {{
var img = document.getElementsByClassName('acc-selector-img r-stretch')[0];
var corrSel = root.querySelector('.acc-corr-select');
var biasSel = root.querySelector('.acc-bias-select');
if (!img || !corrSel || !biasSel) return;
var entry = manifest[corrSel.value];
if (entry && entry[biasSel.value]) {{ img.src = entry[biasSel.value]; }}
}}
root.addEventListener('change', function(e) {{
if (e.target.classList.contains('acc-corr-select') || e.target.classList.contains('acc-bias-select')) {{
update();
}}
}});
}})();
</script>"""
    return "\n".join(line for line in html.splitlines() if line.strip() != "")

manifest = {}
for sim in all_sim_objs.values():
    for idx_corr in range(sim["corr_to_hidden"].size(0)):
        fpath, corr_val, bias_val = plot_acceptance_summary(sim, idx_corr)
        manifest.setdefault(f"{corr_val:.2f}", {})[f"{bias_val:.2f}"] = fpath
```

## Checking out the convergence of the betas

### Differences of logits trained on accepts to trained on full history

```{python}
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection

IMG_DIR_BETAS = CACHED_IMG_DIR + "/betas-per-gen"
os.makedirs(IMG_DIR_BETAS, exist_ok=True)

def plot_betas(
  sim_objs,
  bias_str,
  metric,
  img_dir = IMG_DIR_BETAS
):
  bias_val = sim_objs["bias_prop"]
  fname = f"betas_bias_{bias_val:.2f}_metric_{metric}.png".replace("-", "m")
  fpath = os.path.join(img_dir, fname).replace("\\", "/")

  if os.path.exists(fpath) and USE_CACHED_IMAGES:
    return fpath, bias_val, metric

  saved_betas = torch.load(
        os.path.join(grid_path, 'bias_' + bias_str, 'betas_per_acc_and_gen.pt'),
        map_location='cpu',
        weights_only=False
    )
  betas_all = saved_betas["through_the_door"]
  betas_acc = torch.stack([
          saved_betas[acc_k + '_' + metric]
          for acc_k in ("acc_based", "oracle")
      ],
    dim=0
  )

  beta_diffs = betas_all.unsqueeze(0) - betas_acc

  alpha = 0.6
  y_offset_mul = 0.05
  linewidth = 2

  A, Co, G, K = betas_acc.shape

  fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, K, figsize=(4*K, 4.5 + 0.3))
  #fig.subplots_adjust(bottom=0.2)
  cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab10")
  colors = [cmap(i)[:3] + (alpha,) for i in range(Co) for _ in range(A)]
  line_styles_ao = {0 : "solid", 1 : "dashed", 2 : "dotted"} # [accept_based, oracle]
  line_styles = [line_styles_ao[ao] for i in range(Co) for ao in range(A)]

  for k in range(K):
      ax = axes[k]
      betas_k = beta_diffs[..., k]          # [AO, Co, G]
      gen_round = torch.arange(G)

      # Build segments for LineCollection
      segments = [torch.stack([gen_round, betas_k[ao, co]], dim=-1) for co in range(Co) for ao in range(A)]
      lc = LineCollection(segments, colors=colors, linewidths=linewidth, linestyles=line_styles)

      ax.add_collection(lc)
      ax.set_xlim(0, G-1)
      min_beta, max_beta = betas_k.min().item(), betas_k.max().item()
      add_rest_beta = y_offset_mul * (max_beta - min_beta)
      ax.set_ylim(min_beta - add_rest_beta, max_beta + add_rest_beta)

      #ax.set_title(f"K = {k}")
      ax.set_ylabel(f"$\\beta_{{{k}}}$")
      ax.set_xlabel("Generation round")
      #ax.grid(True)


  handles_corrs = (
    [Line2D([0], [0], linewidth=linewidth, color='k', ls=line_styles_ao[ao]) for ao in range(A)] +
    [Line2D([0], [0], linewidth=linewidth, color=c) for c in colors[::A]]
  )
  labels_corrs = ["Biased Acc.", "Unb. Acc."] + [f"{corr.item():.2f}" for corr in sim_objs["corr_to_hidden"]]



  fig.suptitle(f"$\\pi_b = {sim_objs['bias_prop']}$, Threshold Basis: {metric}", fontsize=14)
  fig.tight_layout()

  fig.subplots_adjust(bottom=0.25)
  fig.legend(
      handles_corrs,
      labels_corrs,
      ncol=len(handles_corrs),
      loc="lower center"
  )

  fig.savefig(fpath, dpi=110, bbox_inches="tight")
  plt.close(fig)
  return fpath, bias_val, metric

def render_betas_selector_html(manifest, container_id,
                                bias_label=r"\pi_b", metric_label="Threshold Basis"):
    bias_values = sorted(manifest.keys(), key=float)
    metric_values = sorted({m for b in manifest.values() for m in b})
    default_bias, default_metric = bias_values[0], metric_values[0]
    default_img = manifest[default_bias][default_metric]

    manifest_json = json.dumps(manifest)
    bias_options = "\n".join(f'<option value="{b}">{b}</option>' for b in bias_values)
    metric_options = "\n".join(f'<option value="{m}">{m}</option>' for m in metric_values)

    html = f"""<figure class="betas-selector" id="{container_id}" data-manifest='{manifest_json}'>
<div class="betas-selector-controls">
<label>${bias_label}$:
<select class="betas-bias-select">{bias_options}</select>
</label>
<label>{metric_label}:
<select class="betas-metric-select">{metric_options}</select>
</label>
</div>
<img class="betas-selector-img" src="{default_img}" />
</figure>
<script>
(function() {{
var root = document.getElementById('{container_id}');
var manifest = JSON.parse(root.getAttribute('data-manifest'));
function update() {{
var img = document.getElementsByClassName('betas-selector-img r-stretch')[0];
```

## How does the surprise look like?

```{python}
#| label: surprise-setup
#| output: false
IMG_DIR_SURPRISE = CACHED_IMG_DIR + "/surprise"
os.makedirs(IMG_DIR_SURPRISE, exist_ok=True)
def plot_surprise(
        sim_objs,
        bias_str,
        w,
        corr_idx,
        grid_path,
        exp_type,
        min_bads_for_valid=4,
        img_dir=IMG_DIR_SURPRISE
):
    corr = sim_objs["corr_to_hidden"][corr_idx].item()
    bias = sim_objs["bias_prop"]

    fname = f"surprise_corr_{corr:.2f}_bias_{bias:.2f}_w{w}_{exp_type}.png".replace("-", "m")
    fpath = os.path.join(img_dir, fname).replace("\\", "/")

    if os.path.exists(fpath) and USE_CACHED_IMAGES:
        return fpath, corr, bias

    future_stats = torch.load(
        os.path.join(grid_path, 'bias_' + bias_str, 'future_expectations_with_window.pt'),
        map_location='cpu',
        weights_only=False
    )

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows = 2, ncols=3, figsize=(17, 8.5))
    gen_round = sim_objs["credit_data"].gen_round
    corr = sim_objs["corr_to_hidden"][corr_idx].item()
    metric_to_name = {"roc" : "AUROC", "ks" : "KS-Statistic"}

    sample_sizes = sim_objs["sample_sizes"]

    for i_m, m in enumerate(METRIC_CATEGORIES):
        acc_flag = sim_objs["alternative_accepted"].get(
          ('acc_based' if exp_type == 'Biased' else 'oracle') + '_' + m,
          sim_objs["credit_data"].accepted
        )[corr_idx, :]
        bad_flag = sim_objs["credit_data"].default_flag[corr_idx, :].to(bool)
        
        G = gen_round[-1].item() + 1

        count_accepts = gen_round.new_zeros((G,)).scatter_add_(
            dim=0,
            index=gen_round,
            src=acc_flag.to(gen_round.dtype)
        )
        cum_sum_acc = count_accepts.cumsum(dim=-1)[:-1]

        count_accepted_bads = gen_round.new_zeros((G,)).scatter_add_(
            dim=0,
            index=gen_round,
            src=(bad_flag & acc_flag).to(gen_round.dtype)
        )
        count_acc_bads_per_window = torch.nn.functional.pad(
            count_accepted_bads, pad=(0,w-1), value=0
        )[torch.arange(G).unsqueeze(-1) + torch.arange(w)].sum(dim=-1)
        invalid_realized_metrics = count_acc_bads_per_window[1:] < min_bads_for_valid

        expectation = sim_objs["stats"][
          ('acc_based' if exp_type == 'Biased' else 'oracle_comparable') + f'_{m}_stats'
        ].mean(dim=(1, 3))[:, corr_idx]
        biased_real_lbl = (
          'biased_acc_' +
          ('acc_based' if exp_type == 'Biased' else 'oracle') +
          f'_{m}_real_{m}'
        )
        real_biased_acc = future_stats[w]['logit'][biased_real_lbl][corr_idx, 1:].masked_fill(
            invalid_realized_metrics, float('nan')
        )
        real_unb_acc = future_stats[w]['logit']['un' + biased_real_lbl][corr_idx, 1:].masked_fill(
            invalid_realized_metrics, float('nan')
        )

        tab10_cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab10")
        colors_for_lines = {
            "expectation" : tab10_cmap(0),
            "real_biased" : tab10_cmap(1),
            "real_unbiased" : tab10_cmap(2),
        }

        N = sample_sizes.size(0)
        idx_for_ticks = [0] + list(range(12, N, 25)) + [N-1]

        ax_abs, ax_diffs, ax_abs_diffs = axes[i_m]

        ax_abs.set_title("Expected vs Realized performance")
        ax_diffs.set_title("Surprise")
        ax_abs_diffs.set_title("Absolute surprise")

        ax_abs.plot(sample_sizes, expectation, label=r"$\mathbb{E}$", color=colors_for_lines["expectation"])
        ax_abs.plot(sample_sizes, real_unb_acc, label="$perf($unb$)$", color=colors_for_lines["real_unbiased"])
        ax_abs.plot(sample_sizes, real_biased_acc, label="$perf($bias$)$", color=colors_for_lines["real_biased"])

        diff_to_unb = expectation - real_unb_acc
        diff_to_biased = expectation - real_biased_acc


        ax_diffs.plot(
            sample_sizes,
            diff_to_unb,
            label=r"$\mathbb{E}$ - $perf($unb$)$",
            color=colors_for_lines["real_unbiased"]
            #s=2
        )
        ax_diffs.plot(
            sample_sizes,
            diff_to_biased,
            label=r"$\mathbb{E}$ - $perf($bias$)$",
            color=colors_for_lines["real_biased"]
            #s=2
        )
        ax_diffs.axhline(y=0, lw=1, ls="dashed", c='gray')

        abs_diff_to_unb = diff_to_unb.abs()
        abs_diff_to_biased = diff_to_biased.abs()

        ax_abs_diffs.plot(sample_sizes, abs_diff_to_unb, label=r"$|\mathbb{E}($bias$)$ - $m($unb$)|$", color=colors_for_lines["real_unbiased"])
        ax_abs_diffs.plot(sample_sizes, abs_diff_to_biased.abs(), label=r"$|\mathbb{E}($bias$)$ - $m($bias$)|$", color=colors_for_lines["real_biased"])

        for ax in axes[i_m]:
            ax.set_ylabel(metric_to_name[m])

    for ax in axes.flatten():
        ax.set_xlabel("Count gen. observations (thousands)")
        ax.set_xticks(sample_sizes[idx_for_ticks])
        ax.set_xticklabels([f"{value/1000:.1f}" for value in sample_sizes[idx_for_ticks].tolist()], rotation=45)
        ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=8)
        ax.legend(ncols=len(ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[0]))

        top_ax = ax.twiny()
        top_ax.set_xlim(ax.get_xlim())
        top_ax.set_xticks(sample_sizes[idx_for_ticks])
        top_ax.set_xticklabels([f"{value/1000:.1f}" for value in cum_sum_acc[idx_for_ticks].tolist()], rotation=45)
        top_ax.set_xlabel("Biased Accepts count (thousands)")
        top_ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=8)

    fig.suptitle(f"$\\pi_b = {sim_objs['bias_prop']}$, $\\sigma_{{mh}}={corr:.2f}$, $W_f$={w}, {exp_type} Accept Policy")

    fig.tight_layout()

    fig.savefig(fpath, dpi=110, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    return fpath, corr, bias

def render_surprise_selector_html(manifest, container_id,
                                   corr_label=r"\sigma_{mh}", bias_label=r"\pi_b",
                                   w_label=r"W_f", exp_label="Exp. Type"):
    corr_values = sorted(manifest.keys(), key=float)
    bias_values = sorted({b for c in manifest.values() for b in c}, key=float)
    w_values = sorted({w for c in manifest.values() for b in c.values() for w in b}, key=int)
    exp_values = sorted({e for c in manifest.values() for b in c.values() for w in b.values() for e in w})

    default_corr, default_bias, default_w = corr_values[0], bias_values[0], w_values[0]
    default_exp = exp_values[0] if exp_values[0] in manifest[default_corr][default_bias][default_w] else next(iter(manifest[default_corr][default_bias][default_w]))
    default_img = manifest[default_corr][default_bias][default_w][default_exp]

    manifest_json = json.dumps(manifest)
    corr_options = "\n".join(f'<option value="{c}">{c}</option>' for c in corr_values)
    bias_options = "\n".join(f'<option value="{b}">{b}</option>' for b in bias_values)
    w_options = "\n".join(f'<option value="{w}">{w}</option>' for w in w_values)
    exp_options = "\n".join(f'<option value="{e}">{e}</option>' for e in exp_values)

    html = f"""<figure class="surprise-selector" id="{container_id}" data-manifest='{manifest_json}'>
<div class="surprise-selector-controls">
<label>${corr_label}$:
<select class="surprise-corr-select">{corr_options}</select>
</label>
<label>${bias_label}$:
<select class="surprise-bias-select">{bias_options}</select>
</label>
<label>${w_label}$:
<select class="surprise-w-select">{w_options}</select>
</label>
<label>{exp_label}:
<select class="surprise-exp-select">{exp_options}</select>
</label>
</div>
<img class="surprise-selector-img" src="{default_img}" />
</figure>
<script>
(function() {{
var root = document.getElementById('{container_id}');
var manifest = JSON.parse(root.getAttribute('data-manifest'));
function update() {{
var img = document.getElementsByClassName('surprise-selector-img r-stretch')[0];
var corrSel = root.querySelector('.surprise-corr-select');
var biasSel = root.querySelector('.surprise-bias-select');
var wSel = root.querySelector('.surprise-w-select');
var expSel = root.querySelector('.surprise-exp-select');
if (!img || !corrSel || !biasSel || !wSel || !expSel) return;
var c = manifest[corrSel.value];
var b = c && c[biasSel.value];
var w = b && b[wSel.value];
var path = w && w[expSel.value];
if (path) {{ img.src = path; }}
}}
root.addEventListener('change', function(e) {{
var cls = e.target.classList;
if (cls.contains('surprise-corr-select') || cls.contains('surprise-bias-select') ||
    cls.contains('surprise-w-select') || cls.contains('surprise-exp-select')) {{
update();
}}
}});
}})();
</script>"""
    return "\n".join(line for line in html.splitlines() if line.strip() != "")

windows = [3, 5, 7, 10]

manifest_surprises = {}
for bias_str, sim in all_sim_objs.items():
    for idx_corr in range(sim["corr_to_hidden"].size(0)):
        for w in windows:
            for exp_type in ["Biased", "Unbiased"]:
                fpath, corr_val, bias_val = plot_surprise(sim, bias_str, w, idx_corr, grid_path, exp_type)
                (manifest_surprises
                    .setdefault(f"{corr_val:.2f}", {})
                    .setdefault(f"{bias_val:.2f}", {})
                    .setdefault(str(w), {}))[exp_type] = fpath

```

# How to do Reinforcement Learning for RI

## In evaluation lies the key

* Biased acceptance policy stabilization in high confidence region.

* Its expectation comes close to its performance in the future unbiased
  accepts.

* If we could infer from the future accepts the unbiased region, we should
  expect the surprise w. r. t. to that region to reduce.

* $\Rightarrow$ Surprise has potential to be used as reward signal,

  * by inferring some lables of the rejected future accepts, specifically
  * as a correction to the estimated probability of default.

## References

:::{#refs}

:::
